title: `TypeError` when requesting `_stcore/metrics` and using `st.connection("sql")`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Requesting `/_stcore/metrics` will throw a `TypeError` if using `st.connection("sql")`.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.connection("sql")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a new Python project, installing `streamlit 1.57.0` and `sqlalchemy 2.0.49`
2. Create a `main.py` and copy the above example into it
3. Create a `.streamlit/secrets.toml` and copy this into it:

```toml
[connections.sql]
url = "sqlite:///:memory:"
```

5. Run `main.py` with `streamlit`
6. Run `curl http://localhost:8501/_stcore/metrics` in another terminal

### Expected Behavior

- No errors in the terminal running Streamlit
- Should return the actual metrics as the response from the `curl` command, something like:

```

# UNIT cache_memory_bytes bytes
# HELP cache_memory_bytes Total memory consumed by a cache.

# TYPE session_events counter
# HELP session_events Total count of session events by type.

# TYPE session_duration_seconds counter
# UNIT session_duration_seconds seconds
# HELP session_duration_seconds Total time spent in active sessions, in seconds.
session_duration_seconds_total 0
# TYPE active_sessions gauge
# HELP active_sessions Current number of active sessions.
active_sessions 2
# EOF
```

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.57.0
- Python version: 3.13.3
- Operating System: Bluefin (Version: 44.20260519)
- Browser: Firefox


### Additional Information

Very similar to #9428, except I used the solution described there with `st.connection`, but the problem still persists.

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15307)

Requesting `/_stcore/metrics` raises a `TypeError: cannot create weak reference to '_EmptyListener' object` whenever a SQLAlchemy `Engine` (here returned by `st.connection("sql")`) lives in the cache. The traceback shows the error originates in `cache_resource_api.CachedResourceFunction.get_stats`, which calls vendored `pympler.asizeof` on every cached entry to compute its byte size. `asizeof` walks attributes via `_dir2`/`hasattr`, which triggers SQLAlchemy's lazy-loading descriptor `_memoized_attr_ref` and tries `weakref.ref(_EmptyListener)`, an object that does not support weak references. The OP correctly notes this is the same underlying bug as #9428 — using `st.connection` doesn't avoid it because `st.connection` is internally backed by `[USER].cache_resource` (see `lib/streamlit/runtime/connection_factory.py`), so the engine still ends up in the resource cache that gets sized for metrics. Likely fix: catch and skip entries that raise during `asizeof` in `CachedResourceFunction.get_stats` (return `0` / log a warning) so a single non-introspectable cached object doesn't break the entire `/_stcore/metrics` endpoint.

### Related Issues

- [#9428 — `TypeError` when requesting `_stcore/metrics` with sqlalchemy engine in session state](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9428): Same root cause and identical traceback; OP explicitly references it. The earlier issue stored the engine in `session_state`; this one reaches the same cache via `st.connection("sql")`. Strong duplicate candidate.
- [#9159 — Add support for instrumentation and observability](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9159): Discusses the broader `_stcore/metrics`/observability story; the brittle `asizeof`-based cache stats computation is a related reliability concern in this area.
- [#8674 — Be able to close cached resources (`[USER].cache_resource`)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8674): Related lifecycle issue around cached SQLAlchemy/DB resources, which underlies why such engines end up in `cache_resource` and trigger this introspection bug.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `claude-opus-4-7-thinking-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Hi! I'd love to pick this up.

The issue stems from asizeof hitting SQLAlchemy's lazy-loading descriptors on objects that don't support weak references. I'll add a safe fallback/try-except block inside CachedResourceFunction.get_stats to catch the TypeError and return 0 for those specific un-sizeable objects, ensuring the rest of the /_stcore/metrics endpoint stays up.

Will drop a PR shortly!
